problem:
Let $K=MN.$ What is the value of ${k}_{12}$, if

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}],\,N=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 \\ -3 & -2 & -5\end{aligned}]?
$$

examples.worked_solution:
Multiplying the $3$rd row in $A$ by the $2$nd column in $B$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{32} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =1\cdot 4+2\cdot (-2) \\  & =4-4 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Here, $S$ is a $1\times 4$ matrix and $T$ is a $4\times 2$ matrix. 

There are $4$ columns in $S$ and $4$ rows in $T,$ so $S$ and $T$ are conformable for multiplication:

$$
{S}_{1\times \boxed{\text{4}}}{\cdot }_{✓}{T}_{\boxed{\text{4}}\times 2}={ST}_{1\times 2}
$$

Let's compute $ST,$ one element at a time:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 4 \\ -2 & 1 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}24 & ∗\end{aligned}], &  & \,24=2\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot 0+1\cdot (-2)+4\cdot 6 \\  & [\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 4 \\ -2 & 1 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}24 & 1\end{aligned}], &  & \,1=2\cdot (-2)+(-3)\cdot 4+1\cdot 1+4\cdot 4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$ST=[\begin{aligned}24 & 1\end{aligned}].$
